concerns.text: Tasks T010 and T011 (Tests for US1) are marked [X] (completed) but appear BEFORE their implementation tasks T012-T018 in the logical flow, and T014 (a prerequisite for T010/T011 logic) is marked [ ]. This violates 'Producer before Consumer' and creates a false state where tests claim to pass logic that hasn't been implemented.

Test tasks T019 and T020 are marked [X] (completed) but depend on implementation tasks T022 and T023 which are marked [ ]. T019 explicitly depends on T022 (convex hull logic) and T020 on T023 (power analysis). Marking tests as complete before their producers are implemented violates the artifact-flow dependency.

Test tasks T030 and T031 are marked [ ] (unstarted) but the implementation tasks they depend on (T032-T038) are also marked [ ]. While the status matches, the ordering is inverted: tests are listed before implementation in the visual block, and the 'Independent Test' section for US3 implies the visualization must work, yet the implementation tasks are unstarted. The block structure confuses the 'Producer before Consumer' flow.

Task T009 (Environment configuration) is marked [ ] (unstarted) but is a prerequisite for T009a (Source Check gating) and T012 (Data Ingestion). T009a depends on T009 to have the URLs configured. The current order implies T009a can run without T009, violating the dependency chain.

The 'Tests for User Story' sections are placed AFTER the implementation blocks but marked with completion status [X] for tasks that depend on unstarted implementation tasks. This creates a semantic contradiction in the task state. Tests should be listed after implementation but marked [ ] until the implementation is complete.
